info.bio:
Britney Jean Spears nació el 2 de diciembre de 1981, en McComb,  pero la mayor parte de su infancia la pasó en un pueblo muy pequeño, de 2.659 habitantes llamado Kentwood, en Louisiana. Allí se crió junto a su abuela, sus padres y sus dos hermanos

Conocida como la "Princesa del Pop" ha cosechado éxito desde el lanzamiento de su primer sencillo ...Baby One More Time. Entre sus otros éxitos están (You Drive Me) Crazy, Oops!...I Did It Again

podcast.title: 1996 Pop Resurgence
podcast.body: Britney Spears was a key figure in the resurgence of pop music, which started flexing its muscles again around 1996 and challenged the dominance of rock acts on the music charts. "pop started flexing its muscles again, spice girls, Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys, Mariah Carey, and Sink."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Ruling the Charts (1998-1999)
podcast.body: Britney Spears is cited as a prominent example of "teen pop by White Axe" that was "ruling the charts in 1998 and 1999." This era of music began to wane by 2002 and 2003. "Of course, teen pop by White Axe was also ruling the charts in 1998 and 1999, including Britney Spears, and Christina Aguilera."

srcs.episode: Raise Your Glass Edition Part 1

srcs.episode: Raise Your Glass Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Debut in 1999
podcast.body: Britney Spears' debut in 1999 marked a turning point for teen pop, a genre that had not been well-regarded since Madonna grew older with her audience in the mid-80s. "Cuando Britney Spears en 1999, yo creo que pasaba una cosa y es que todo el pop-up adolescente, casi desde que Madonna había envejecido con su público durante mitad de los 80, no había sido la música mejor tratada, no había sido el público mejor tratado."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Dominated Teen Pop (1999)
podcast.body: Britney Spears was a dominant force in teen pop in 1999, a year also heavily influenced by groups like Backstreet Boys and Latin pop artists. "1999, a year dominated by teen pop by Britney Spears and Backstreet Boys."

podcast.title: Target of Justin Timberlake's "Cry Me a River" (2002)
podcast.body: Britney Spears was the subject of Justin Timberlake's "very thinly veiled kiss off" in his 2002 hit "Cry Me a River." The accompanying music video even "starred a blonde Spears look alike," leaving little doubt about the song's inspiration and making the diss highly public. "Cry Me a River was also a very thinly veiled kiss off to Justin Timberlake's former girlfriend, Brittany Spears."

podcast.title: Pioneering Pop Star Residency in Las Vegas (2013-2017)
podcast.body: Britney Spears became the first mainstream pop star to sign a multi-year residency deal in Las Vegas, performing at Planet Hollywood from 2013 to 2017. Her success sparked a new trend for pop artists in Vegas, diversifying the city's entertainment beyond gambling and demonstrating the viability of long-term engagements for contemporary musicians. "She was the first mainstream pop star to sign a multi-year residency, 2013 to 2017. She sparked a new trend for pop stars in Vegas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: Return to Top 100 via Las Vegas Residency (2016)
podcast.body: Britney Spears re-entered the Top 100 earners list at position 89 after years of being largely absent. This resurgence was primarily fueled by her Las Vegas concerts, which provided a significant source of income. "sus conciertos también en las vegas, le han dado un enorme fuente de ingresos que la vuelta meten el ranking to 100 después de muchísimo tiempo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Los artistas que más dinero han ganado este año y por qué.

podcast.title: Bipolar Disorder
podcast.body: Britney Spears is included in a list of musicians suffering from bipolar disorder. "Lou Reed, Axel Rose, Shenandoah Conner, Scott Wyland, rapper Chris Brown, Matthew Good, Adam Ant, Brittany Spears, Jack Irons, former drummer with the Chili Peppers, Scott Stap of Creed, Pete Wentz of Fallout Boy, Frank Sinatra."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Health Issues of Musicians

podcast.title: Bubblegum Music Resurgence
podcast.body: Britney Spears was one of the artists who represented the resurgence of Bubblegum Music in the late 1990s and early 21st century. Her success contributed to this genre's renewed popularity. "It would rise again in the late 90s and into the early 21st century with the likes of Britney Spears and the Spice Girls and NSYNC and the like."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.title: Catalyst for a New Generation of Solo Artists
podcast.body: Britney Spears is recognized as the pivotal figure who marked the shift from boy and girl bands dominating the charts to a new wave of successful solo teen pop artists, paving the way for figures like Avril Lavigne. "Britney Spears... la persona que marca la ruptura de las vois y las guia de spam a las listas y los solicitas del pop-up de la extente."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Electronica as Alternative Music Savior (Late 1990s)
podcast.body: Electronica was seen by critics in the late 1990s as the potential savior for alternative music from the perceived ruin caused by pop acts like the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears. "This, the critic said, was going to be the thing that saved the world of alternative music from ruin at the hands of the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears and their ilk in the late 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 500th Show!

podcast.title: Guantanamo Bay Torture
podcast.body: Tracks by Britney Spears were part of the unofficial torture playlist at Camp Delta, the military prison at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba. Interrogators would use whatever music was available or amused them to break prisoners. "The torture playlist there also included March of the Pigs from 9-Inch Nails. We are the champions from Queen, Springsteens born in the USA, Angel of Death from Slayer, Metallica's won, and tracks from Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Using Music as a Weapon

podcast.title: Historical Figure and Trendsetter
podcast.body: Britney Spears is recognized as a historical figure in music, marking a significant shift in musical trends from boy and girl bands to solo teen artists. "Brindespir ya es un personaje histórico de la música y marca un cambio importante en la tendencia musical de las vois y las Getsfans a todas las artizas o de extentes en solitario."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Hits Composed by Max Martin
podcast.body: Many of Britney Spears' hits, like those of other teen pop stars, were composed by Max Martin, who was a prolific hitmaker for the genre. "Britney Spears fue el tío que luego acabó componiendo todos los éxitos y todas estas estrellas del pop-up de la extente."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Initial Label Rejections
podcast.body: Despite her eventual success, Britney Spears was initially rejected by several record labels before one finally decided to invest in her career. "Britney Spears fue rechazada por varias discográficas hasta que consiguió que alguien apostara por ella."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Leading Pop Stars in Late 1990s
podcast.body: Within a few years of the Spice Girls' emergence, Britney Spears became one of the biggest popular music stars in the world, representing the strong comeback of pop music that continued to be absolutely huge until about 2001. "It began with the spice girls, but within a few years, the biggest popular music stars in the world were a bunch of boy bands and singers like Britney Spears."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

podcast.title: Market Revolution in US and UK
podcast.body: The release of Britney Spears' debut album in January 1999 was a groundbreaking success, described as a revolution in the music market in the United States and the United Kingdom, and almost globally. "el mercado musical en Estados Unidos en Reino Unido casi en el mundo entero, pero en Estados Unidos es la revolución."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Massive Album Sales
podcast.body: Britney Spears achieved immense commercial success, selling tens of millions of albums, a feat undoubtedly aided by her visually impactful and high-budget music videos. These sales highlighted the effectiveness of her promotional strategies during her peak. "And Britney sold tens of millions of albums as a result."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.title: Max Martin Episode Reference
podcast.body: Max Martin, the Swedish pop mastermind, was discussed at length in an episode of "Hit Parade" specifically dedicated to Britney Spears. "whom we discussed at length in our Britney Spears episode of Hit Parade."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Raise Your Glass Edition Part 2

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Raise Your Glass Edition Part 2

podcast.title: Million-Dollar Music Video Production (2010s)
podcast.body: In an era where music video budgets significantly shrunk, Britney Spears was noted as one of the few artists who still released videos with production costs exceeding a million dollars during the 2010s. This suggests a continued commitment to large-scale video productions. "There were some exceptions in the 2010s, both Madonna and Britney Spears had videos that topped a million dollars in production costs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 5: Music and Tech

podcast.title: New Generation's Preference
podcast.body: Britney Spears was among the artists preferred by a younger generation of music fans coming of age after the Britpop era, signaling a move towards more commercial pop music. "And you know what they wanted? Ice Girls. Britney Spears. Robbie Williams."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: New Millennium Sex Symbol
podcast.body: Britney Spears was portrayed, "for better or worse," as the new sex symbol of the new millennium. Her image and music videos played a significant role in this perception, often featuring high production values that supported her pop superstar status. "For better or worse, she was portrayed as the new sex symbol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.title: Perceived Threat to Rock Music
podcast.body: Britney Spears was mentioned as part of the pop music landscape that, along with boy bands, seemed poised to "swamp" rock music before The Strokes helped to revitalize the genre. "when it looked like we were going to be swamped by boy bands and Britney Spears."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Trying to be a Superstar in the 21st Century

podcast.title: Pioneer of Her Generation
podcast.body: Britney Spears is considered the true beginning and the original pioneer of her generation of teen pop stars, launching her debut album in 1999, slightly preceding Christina Aguilera's release in the same year. "Britney Spears fue la primera y fue la original."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Piracy Deterrence off Somalia
podcast.body: Crews of ships harassed by pirates off the coast of Somalia discovered that blasting Britney Spears music, particularly "One More Time" and "Oops, I Did It Again" on a loop, seemed to effectively ward off imminent attacks. "Some of the crews of these ships discovered that when an attack is imminent, blasting the pirates with Britney Spears seems to ward them off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Using Music as a Weapon

podcast.title: Pirate Deterrent
podcast.body: British Navy members successfully repelled Somali pirates off the East Coast of Africa by playing Britney Spears' songs, specifically "Oops!... I Did It Again" and "...Baby One More Time." "Oops, I did it again, and baby one more time, seemed to do the trick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

podcast.title: Pop Music Decline
podcast.body: Britney Spears symbolized the pop music landscape of the mid-90s. As her initial fanbase aged and sought music that reflected their anger and frustrations, it created an opening for bands like Alexis on Fire to gain mainstream traction. "But during that time, we were seeing the end of the spike in pop music, you know, the back street boys and instincts and Christine Aguilar is in Britney Spears and that group of people who had been into pop since the middle 90s with spice girls and whatever, they were now getting older and they were getting angry and they were looking for something that spoke to that anger and their fears and their frustrations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

podcast.title: Post-Eurodance Popularity (New Millennium)
podcast.body: Britney Spears was a prominent pop artist whose music dominated the charts and television airwaves in the new millennium. Her rise coincided with channels like MTV shifting away from Eurodance in favor of American pop and other genres. "...Britney Spears..."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La gran mentira detrás del Eurodance

podcast.title: Recording Debut Album in Sweden
podcast.body: Despite being American and very young, Britney Spears recorded her debut album, `...Baby One More Time`, in Sweden, collaborating with several Swedish composers for its creation. "cómo Britney Spears es noamericana, siendo tan joven, se va a suecir a grabar el disco y cómo tiene varios compositores suecos del trase del Baby One More Time."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Rise of Pop Music
podcast.body: Britney Spears was among the pop artists that defined the musical tastes of Generation Y towards the end of the 1990s, reflecting a shift away from brooding grunge and post-punk alt-rock. "This cheerful generation led us to an era of spice girls and backstreet boys in sync, Britney Spears."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 9: The Festivals

podcast.title: Sampling of Funky Drummer Break
podcast.body: Britney Spears is listed among the diverse artists who have sampled Clyde Stubblefield's drum break from James Brown's "Funky Drummer." "But also Ed Sheeran, Britney Spears, Nine Inch Nails, Kenny G, Stone Roses, Poppullet itself, and Shanato Conner."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Unsung Heroes of Music: Part 2

podcast.title: Significant Figure in Music History
podcast.body: Britney Spears was an extremely important figure in music over the last 30 years, not just herself, but her entire generation of teen pop artists, from a discographic and market perspective. "Britney Spears fue una persona importantísima los últimos 30 años en música."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Poniendo a Britney Spears en su lugar

podcast.title: Transition to Solo Career
podcast.body: After leaving Disney Channel, Britney Spears, along with Christina Aguilera and others, attempted to launch solo careers in a market predominantly defined by boy and girl bands. "después de que toda esa generación abandonase el Disney Channel en Estados Unidos, Britney Spears fue una de ellas, no solo y hasta Cristina Guilera varias intentaron lanzar sus carreras en solitario, pero era la generación de las Boys y las Yels Bans."

podcast.title: Use of Vintage 80s Sounds
podcast.body: Her music, among other pop artists seeking fresh sounds, incorporated vintage 80s sounds. Producers, tired of contemporary digital keyboard sounds, looked back to the 80s for inspiration. "This continued with songs from people like Britney Spears. Pop artists who were looking for new fresh sounds, used producers who were tired of all the available digital keyboard sounds of the day, so they started looking back at the 80s for old vintage sounds."

podcast.title: Youth Identity Expression - 1990s
podcast.body: In the 1990s, young people expressed their identity and tastes by filling their rooms with posters of artists like Britney Spears. This was part of a broader cultural trend where urban tribes lived their golden age, using various methods to show their individuality. "o llenando su habitación de posters de blindy spills o las espais grales."

xref.title: Electronica as Alternative Music Savior (Late 1990s)
xref.body: Electronica was seen by critics in the late 1990s as the potential savior for alternative music from the perceived ruin caused by pop acts like the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears. "This, the critic said, was going to be the thing that saved the world of alternative music from ruin at the hands of the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears and their ilk in the late 1990s."

xref.title: Glamour in Pop Music Videos
xref.body: The Backstreet Boys were part of a trend in the mid to late 1990s where glamour returned to pop music, characterized by expensive videos. This marked a contrast to the anti-fashion ethos that emerged from the alt-rock revolution. "Glamour returned to pop music with expensive videos from Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys, and InSync."

xref.title: Guantanamo Bay Torture
xref.body: Tracks by Christina Aguilera were included in the unofficial torture playlist at Camp Delta, the military prison at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba. Interrogators selected music that was either readily available or simply amused them for "enhanced interrogation." "The torture playlist there also included March of the Pigs from 9-Inch Nails. We are the champions from Queen, Springsteens born in the USA, Angel of Death from Slayer, Metallica's won, and tracks from Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera."

xref.title: Million-Dollar Music Video Production (2010s)
xref.body: Despite a general trend of decreasing music video budgets in the 2010s due to technology, Madonna was one of the exceptions, producing videos that still topped a million dollars in production costs. This indicates her continued investment in high-budget visual content even as industry norms shifted. "There were some exceptions in the 2010s, both Madonna and Britney Spears had videos that topped a million dollars in production costs."

xref.title: Pop Music Decline
xref.body: The Backstreet Boys were part of a group of pop artists from the mid-90s whose audience, by the mid-2000s, had grown older and began seeking angrier, more expressive music. This shift contributed to the rise of bands like Alexis on Fire. "But during that time, we were seeing the end of the spike in pop music, you know, the back street boys and instincts and Christine Aguilar is in Britney Spears and that group of people who had been into pop since the middle 90s with spice girls and whatever, they were now getting older and they were getting angry and they were looking for something that spoke to that anger and their fears and their frustrations."

xref.title: Pop Music Shift
xref.body: The rise of Alexis on Fire and similar aggressive bands coincided with a shift in pop music in the mid-2000s. Fans who had grown up with pop acts like Backstreet Boys, N'Sync, Christina Aguilera, and Britney Spears from the mid-90s were aging and seeking music that expressed anger, fears, and frustrations, creating an opening for bands like Alexis on Fire and Billy Talent. "But during that time, we were seeing the end of the spike in pop music, you know, the back street boys and instincts and Christine Aguilar is in Britney Spears and that group of people who had been into pop since the middle 90s with spice girls and whatever, they were now getting older and they were getting angry and they were looking for something that spoke to that anger and their fears and their frustrations."

xref.title: Rib Removal Rumor – Denied; Floating Ribs Can Be Surgically Removed but Manson Did Not Have It Done
xref.body: One of the most enduring Marilyn Manson rumors is that he had his lowest ribs removed to facilitate auto-erotic self-gratification. Floating ribs (numbers 11 and 12) do not extend all the way around to the breastbone and can be surgically removed — a procedure sometimes done for women alongside tummy tucks to create an hourglass figure. The same rumor has been attributed to Cher, Pamela Anderson, Kate Moss, Janet Jackson, and Britney Spears. However, Manson categorically did not have this done. The rumor persists purely because he has never worked to dispel the myth, preferring to let the mystery stand. "Because Manson is so weird in the first place, it's understandable why people would believe this rumor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
